descriptor: Pan-European logistics REIT · reported in GBP · quoted in GBp (pence) · subject to a recommended Prologis scheme of arrangement (shareholder-approved, pending regulatory sanction)

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

charts.title: Loan-to-Value
charts.annotation: FY-only: LTV is disclosed at both year-end and half-year, but a mixed FY/H1 series on one axis overstates the swing -- see the DCF for the latest balance-sheet date.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For SEGRO plc: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For SEGRO plc: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For SEGRO plc: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For SEGRO plc: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For SEGRO plc: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nta.title: EPRA NTA & NAV per share
nta.content:
EPRA NTA (net tangible assets) per share strips out items like the mark-to-market of interest-rate swaps that EPRA judges non-cash and non-recurring; NAV is the broader, un-adjusted book value. Both are in pence.

For SEGRO: NTA peaked above 1,100p in FY2021 at the top of the industrial-property cycle, then fell with cap-rate expansion through FY2023 before stabilising around 900-925p. Prologis's cash alternative (1,031.7p) and blended consideration (~933p as of 2026-10-09) sit close to the latest NTA, so the scheme is pricing the portfolio near book, not at a takeover premium to it.

What to watch:

  • Discount or premium of the deal consideration to NTA
  • NTA growth from revaluations versus retained cash
  • EPRA also discloses NDV and NRV per share (in the kpis table, not yet a CSV column) -- NRV assumes no exit from the portfolio, NDV adjusts for deferred tax and debt mark-to-market

ltv.title: Loan-to-value
ltv.content:
LTV is net debt divided by the value of the property portfolio -- the REIT's core leverage covenant metric, distinct from a net-debt/EBITDA ratio.

For SEGRO: LTV has run in the mid-20s to mid-30s% since FY2021, rising as valuations fell in FY2022-23 and easing as the portfolio recovered. A pending all-share/cash acquirer (Prologis) typically targets a stable LTV band going into completion rather than funding growth with incremental leverage.

What to watch:

  • LTV drifting toward covenant ceilings disclosed in the filings
  • Whether LTV moves are driven by debt raised or by valuation swings in the denominator

epraEarnings.title: EPRA earnings & EPRA EPS
epraEarnings.content:
EPRA earnings is recurring profit from the core property business -- rental income less costs and financing -- excluding fair-value movements and gains on disposal that swing statutory net income. EPRA EPS is that figure per share, the number SEGRO's dividend policy is actually set against.

For SEGRO: EPRA earnings have grown every year shown (FY2020 £292m to FY2025 £495m) even through the FY2022-23 valuation downturn, because the valuation swings that hit statutory NetIncome (see Growth & Profitability) don't pass through this measure -- it is the cleaner read on the underlying letting business.

What to watch:

  • EPRA EPS growth versus the dividend per share
  • Divergence between EPRA earnings and statutory net income is valuation-driven, not operating

developmentCapex.title: Total cash capital expenditure
developmentCapex.content:
Total cash capex is SEGRO's own broader disclosure of cash spent on property purchases and development, wider than the generic CapEx line elsewhere on this dashboard.

For SEGRO: spend peaked above £1.7bn in FY2021 at the height of the logistics development cycle and has fallen every year since to £473m in FY2025, consistent with a development-heavy REIT slowing land acquisition and new starts as it approaches the Prologis scheme rather than committing fresh capital to multi-year projects.

What to watch:

  • Capex trending toward maintenance-only levels ahead of a change of control
  • Property disposal proceeds (in the kpis table) funding this spend rather than new debt

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For SEGRO plc: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For SEGRO plc: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

rental.title: Gross vs net rental income
rental.content:
Gross rental income is rent received from tenants before property costs; net rental income deducts void costs, service-charge shortfalls and other direct property expenses -- the EPRA-style NRI margin is net divided by gross.

For SEGRO: the NRI margin has held close to 85% through FY2022-FY2025 despite the vacancy rate drifting up from 3.2% (FY2021) to 6.0% (FY2024) before easing to 5.1% (FY2025) -- EPRA vacancy rate and like-for-like NRI growth are disclosed (in the kpis table) but not yet CSV columns, so aren't charted directly here.

What to watch:

  • Gap between gross and net widening (rising void costs)
  • Like-for-like rental growth versus growth from new developments/acquisitions

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For SEGRO plc: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For SEGRO plc: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
